# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

UPON the day that the last scores for every test were scheduled for display on the Regent’s notice board, Nell alongside Odette traversed the road in each other's company. Grinning and joyful, Odette felt relieved that testing had concluded, feeling pleasantly certain of having secured a passing mark minimum; additional worries did not disturb Odette in the least; possessing no grand aspirations, she remained undisturbed by the agitation that accompanies them. Indeed, a cost attaches to every object we obtain or accept throughout life; while aspirations remain truly valuable to possess, their acquisition comes at a high cost, demanding their required payments of effort, abstaining from pleasure, worry, and disheartenment. Colorless and silent, Nell realized that within another ten minutes' time, the identity of the medal recipient as well as the Avery winner would be revealed to her. Past those coming ten minutes, there appeared to be no duration, right at that moment, deserving of the name Time.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0000 }

“Naturally, you will secure one among them regardless,” remarked Odette, who failed to comprehend how the faculty could possess such bias as to mandate a different outcome.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0001 }

“I don’t hold out any hope for the Avery,” Nell remarked. “The general opinion is that Emily Clay is going to be the winner. There’s no way I’m walking right up to that bulletin board to check it in front of the whole crowd. My moral courage isn’t up to it. My plan is to head directly to the girls’ dressing room. Odette, you have to look at the announcements and bring the news to me afterwards. For the sake of our longstanding friendship, I beg you to make it as fast as you can. Should I have lost, simply state it plain, rather than attempting to soften the blow; and under no circumstances offer me sympathy. Give me your word on this, Odette.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0002 }

Odette made a solemn pledge; nevertheless, as things turned out, no such vow was needed. Upon ascending the front steps at Regent’s, the hall met their eyes filled with schoolboys hoisting Hugh Carrow onto their shoulders while shouting with all their might, “Hurrah for Carrow, Medalist!”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0003 }

Nell experienced a single nauseating wave of failure and letdown briefly. Thus, she had lost while Hugh had triumphed! Ah, Obed would feel regret—he possessed such certainty regarding her victory.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0004 }

And then!
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0005 }

A person shouted:
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0006 }

“Hip, hip, hooray for Miss Harcourt, who has taken the Avery!”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0007 }

“Oh, Nell,” Odette panted, while enthusiastic applause accompanied them on their flight toward the dressing room for girls. “Oh, Nell I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0008 }

And after that, the girls surrounded them, making Nell the middle of a merry, well-wishing crowd. Her hands were gripped firmly, and her shoulders were slapped. She was yanked, jostled, and embraced, yet amidst the commotion, she succeeded in murmuring to Odette:
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0009 }

“Oh, Obed and Thirza are going to be so happy! I have to send a letter with the news to my family immediately.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0010 }

The following significant event was commencement. In the large assembly hall of the Academy, the ceremonies took place. Speeches were delivered, compositions recited, vocal pieces performed, and the public presentation of diplomas, honors, and medals occurred.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0011 }

Obed and Thirza stood present, their sight and hearing consumed by a single scholar upon the stage—a towering young woman dressed in soft green, whose face bore a gentle blush and whose eyes shone like stars, who delivered the finest paper and whom others indicated and spoke of in hushed tones as the Avery victor.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0012 }

“Guess you're pleased we retained her, Thirza?” murmured Obed, breaking his silence for the first time since coming into the room, after Nell had concluded her composition.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0013 }

“I’ve felt relieved on previous occasions as well,” Thirza fired back. “You certainly enjoy dwelling on things, Obed Abernethy.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0014 }

Positioned in the seat behind the pair, Miss Pembroke bent towards them and jabbed Thirza’s back using her parasol.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0015 }

“Does that Nell-girl not make you proud? She makes me proud,” she stated.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0016 }

Nell returned to Brierley alongside Obed and Thirza during that evening. Having been away from home since April, she felt an urgency that prevented her from waiting even one more day. The blossoms on the apple trees had bloomed, making the world appear young and fresh. Isolde was present at Grey Shutters so that she could meet her. Within her private white room, in which a flowering house rose had been placed on the window sill by Thirza, Nell surveyed her surroundings and inhaled a deep, joyful breath.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0017 }

“Oh, Isolde, returning here feels so wonderful. Watching those pointed firs silhouetted against the pink sky is truly wonderful—along with that white orchard and the old Frost Maiden. Doesn't the mint smell delightful? As for that tea rose—well, it combines a song, a hope, and a prayer into a single thing. And seeing you once more is so good, Isolde!”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0018 }

“It was my impression that Mabel Colby was more to your liking than I was,” Isolde uttered with a tone of reproach. “I was informed by Flossie Tulk that this was so. According to Flossie, you were completely taken with her.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0019 }

Laughter escaping her, Nell threw the wilted "June lilies" from her bouquet at Isolde.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0020 }

“Other than a single person, Mabel Colby is the most precious girl in existence, and that one person is you, Isolde,” she stated. “My love for you is greater than it has ever been—and I have a great deal to share with you. However, at this moment, simply sitting in this spot and gazing at you seems like sufficient happiness. It occurs to me that I am weary—weary of my scholarly pursuits and aspirations. Tomorrow, I intend to devote a minimum of two hours to reclining on the grass in the orchard, allowing my mind to remain entirely blank.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0021 }

“You have performed wonderfully, Nell. I imagine you will not continue teaching now that the Avery has been awarded to you?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0022 }

“No. I am headed to Wexcombe come September. Does it not sound marvelous? After three splendid, sunlit months off, I will possess a fresh store of drive by then. Odette and Opal intend to teach. Is it not fantastic to consider that every one of us passed, even extending to Elias Purdy and Flossie Tulk?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0023 }

“Odette has already been offered their school by the Stonebridge trustees,” Isolde said. “Furthermore, Hugh Carrow will be teaching. It is necessary for him. After all, his father is unable to pay for him to attend college next year, which means he intends to cover his own expenses. Should Miss Ames choose to depart, I anticipate he will secure the school here.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0024 }

A strange, subtle feeling of startled disappointment came over Nell. This was news to her; her assumption had been that Hugh's destination was likewise Wexcombe. How would she manage in the absence of their motivating competition? Wouldn't studying—even inside a coeducational institution offering the possibility of an actual degree—feel somewhat dull if her friendly foe was missing?
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0025 }

While eating breakfast the following morning, it occurred to Nell all at once that Obed appeared unwell. Without a doubt, his hair had turned far grayer than it was twelve months prior.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0026 }

“Thirza,” she asked with hesitation once he had left, “is Obed quite well?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0027 }

“No, he isn’t,” Thirza answered anxiously. “His heart has given him a lot of trouble this spring and he refuses to take things easy. He’s caused me a great deal of worry, though he has improved a bit lately and our hired man is reliable, so my hope is that he will take a break and regain his strength. Having you back might help him do that. You have always lifted his spirits.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0028 }

Reaching over the table, Nell cupped Thirza’s face with her hands.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0029 }

“Thirza, your own appearance is not as healthy as I would prefer, either. Fatigue shows on your face. It worries me that your labor has been excessive. Now that my return has occurred, resting is imperative for you. My intention is merely to spend this single day away from work, visiting every beloved familiar location and searching for the dreams of my past, after which you shall have the opportunity to relax while the labor becomes my responsibility.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0030 }

Thirza gave her daughter a loving smile.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0031 }

“It isn’t the labor—it’s my head. Frequently now, I suffer from an ache—behind my eyes. Glasses have been tried on me by Doctor Tranter, yet they fail to help me. At the end of June, a prominent oculist is visiting the Island, and the doctor insists that I consult him. I suppose it will be necessary. Reading or sewing cannot be done comfortably by me anymore. Well, Nell, it must be said that you performed truly well at Regent’s. Taking a First Class License within a single year alongside winning the Avery scholarship—well, well, pride goes before a fall according to Mrs. Sowerby, who disbelieves in women’s higher education entirely; she claims that it renders them unfit for the true sphere of a woman. Not one word of that is believed by me. Mentioning Agatha brings it to my mind—have any updates concerning the Abbey Bank reached you recently, Nell?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0032 }

“I was told it was unstable,” Nell replied. “For what reason?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0033 }

“Agatha stated that very thing. Having come up here on a day during the previous week, she mentioned that people were discussing it. Obed became genuinely anxious. Everything we have put away—to the last cent—is held in that bank. Originally, my desire was for Obed to deposit it into the Savings Bank, yet old Mr. Abbey had been a close friend of father’s, and father had constantly done his banking through him. Obed declared that whatever bank had him as its leader was sufficiently reliable for anyone.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0034 }

“In my opinion, he has merely been its leader in name for a long time,” Nell said. “Being an exceptionally aged man, the institution is actually run by his nephews.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0035 }

“Indeed, once Agatha mentioned that to us, my desire was for Obed to withdraw our funds immediately, a course of action he promised to consider. However, yesterday Mr. Russell assured him that the bank’s condition was secure.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0036 }

Nell experienced her favorable day amid the company of nature. That day remained forever in her memory; it possessed such radiance, golden beauty, and fairness, being entirely unshaded and abundant with blooms. Nell passed several of its plentiful hours within the orchard; her journey took her to the Nymph’s Well, Reedmere, and Primrose Dell; she paid a visit to the manse where she engaged in a fulfilling conversation with Mrs. Wace; and ultimately, when night approached, she accompanied Obed to retrieve the cows, traveling by way of Lovers’ Lane toward the rear pasture. The forest was thoroughly illuminated by the sunset, whose gentle brilliance poured down from the western openings between the hills. Walking deliberately with his head bowed, Obed moved alongside Nell, who was tall and upright, adjusting her elastic stride to match his own.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0037 }

“You have overexerted yourself today, Obed,” she said in a chiding tone. “Why don’t you take it easier?”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0038 }

“Well now, I seem unable to,” remarked Obed, opening the gate to the yard so the cows could pass. “Nell, it is just that my age is catching up with me, causing me to constantly forget. Ah well, my life has been one of fairly hard labor, and my preference is to die while still working.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0039 }

“Had I been the lad you requested,” Nell remarked mournfully, “I could assist you so greatly at present and save you effort in numerous manners. For that single reason, I could truly desire to have been one.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0040 }

“Indeed, I prefer your company over twelve sons, Nell,” Obed stated while tapping her fingers softly. “Always remember that—preferable to twelve sons. Furthermore, a son did not win the Avery scholarship, correct? A daughter won it—my own daughter—a daughter who fills me with pride.”
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0041 }

As he entered the yard, he offered her his timid smile. Nell carried the recollection of it with her when she retired to her room that evening and sat beside her open window for a extended period, dwelling on times gone by and imagining what was to come. In the moonlit light outside, the Frost Maiden appeared hazily white, while the frogs sang in the marsh past Pear Hill. The quiet, silver splendour and sweet-scented stillness of that evening remained in Nell’s memory forever. It marked the final night before grief reached her existence; and once that chilling, hallowing influence has been placed upon a life, it is never entirely the same.
{: #nw-v01-c36-p0042 }
